items.quote: 007: First Light is not just a great James Bond franchise game — it is one of the best products in the franchise's history and one of the best games of 2026. The game is fun from start to finish, with a great story, extremely charismatic characters, and action and stealth in just the right measure. Highly recommended.

007 First Light does something I honestly wasn’t expecting anymore: it makes James Bond feel important in video games again. Not just as another decent licensed title you finish once and forget a few months later, but as a real AAA solo blockbuster that feels ambitious, polished, cinematic, and clearly built by people who genuinely understand what makes 007 special. IO Interactive absolutely nails that balance between stealth, elegance, brutal action, espionage, gadgets, political tension, and pure spectacle without ever turning Bond into some generic action hero. He still feels like James Bond, and that’s probably the game’s biggest success…And yeah, it’s impossible not to think about Uncharted 4 while playing. The animations, pacing, set pieces, and attention to detail constantly give the game that interactive movie feeling we barely see anymore. But what really makes First Light stand out is how it mixes that cinematic approach with some lighter Hitman DNA. Missions give you freedom. You can improvise, sneak around, manipulate enemies, use gadgets creatively, or just let things spiral into chaos. IO Interactive didn’t throw away what made Hitman work. They adapted it to Bond in a really smart way. What really ties everything together though is this younger version of Bond himself. He’s less confident, more impulsive, still figuring himself out, and that origin story angle works incredibly well…Patrick Gibson absolutely crushes it in the role and honestly feels more convincing as the next Bond than half the names currently rumored for the movies. Sure, the AI can be inconsistent at times and some mechanics are simplified, but the game’s energy, variety, and overall sense of spectacle make those flaws easy to overlook. After thirteen years away, 007 honestly couldn’t have asked for a better comeback.

With 007 First Light, IO Interactive brings James Bond back to video games with an experience that perfectly captures the fantasy of Agent 007. Its blend of cinematic storytelling, stealth, combat, and driving creates an elegant, explosive, and consistently thrilling adventure. The result is one of the strongest titles of the year, a game that modernizes the classic essence of Bond and positions itself as a serious contender for awards season.
007 First Light has everything it takes to become a brilliant franchise: presence, gameplay, its own distinct style, and above all, a well-crafted narrative that elevates the James Bond iconography.
Bond is back and he's in fine form. 007 First Light is an excellent stealth game, and a brilliant James Bond game, offering up the best 007 experience in franchise history.

In a year where major releases often arrive broken or soulless, 007 First Light stands out for doing the basics extraordinarily well: telling a good story, introducing characters that matter, and leaving the player wanting more. If this is the beginning of a new era for Bond in games, the future looks very promising.

007 First Light isn’t just a great Bond game – it’s one of the best action-adventure games released this decade. Witnessing the birth of the 007 legend through Bond’s eyes from the beginning is a tale that was long overdue for a video game adaptation, and IO Interactive has pulled it off flawlessly. Tie this origin story in with gameplay systems that prioritize the precision and creativity that 007 is known for, and you have what amounts to one of the best iterations of James Bond that we have seen in recent memory.

By deftly combining its stealth-sim expertise from the Hitman franchise with big-budget, blockbuster sensibilities, IO Interactive has crafted a stellar action espionage romp. Most of all, it’s a reverence for the source material, and a willingness to tell new Bond stories, that elevates 007 First Light to greatness.

007: First Light is a title that fans of the 007 franchise definitely needed. It is a near-perfect simulation of a James Bond video game, complete with engaging gameplay, great presentation, and a compelling narrative that encapsulates the franchise’s identity. It is, without a doubt, the best 007 game of all time, and no other game in the franchise comes close.

IO Interactive feels like they've found a new home in the James Bond franchise. 007 First Light is a blast, with a tense and enthralling narrative that punches way higher and harder than anyone could have expected.
